# The Project {.unnumbered}

Welcome to the course notes for **Health Data Science: AI and Knowledge Translation**.

This platform bridges the gap between traditional epidemiology and modern data science. Unlike standard textbooks that focus on a single language, this resource adopts a **"Polyglot"** approach—teaching R and Python side-by-side—and integrates **Artificial Intelligence** directly into the workflow.

Whether you are a health researcher looking to modernize your skills or a data scientist seeking to understand epidemiological rigor, you are in the right place.

Here, we offer:

-   **"Zero to AI Co-Pilot" Training**: Learn to use Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate, debug, and translate code while critically auditing them for bias and hallucinations.
-   **Real-World Data**: Guides on navigating "messy" open data sources such as NHANES and WHO, rather than sanitized "toy" datasets.
-   **Knowledge Translation**: Step-by-step walkthroughs on building interactive dashboards (Shiny/Dash) and dynamic reports to communicate findings to policymakers.

## What We Aim to Achieve {.unnumbered}

We are on a mission to:

-   **Democratize Compute Access**: Eliminate hardware barriers by using cloud-native environments (Google Colab, Kaggle) that run on any device.
-   **Bridge the "Polyglot" Gap**: Provide "Rosetta Stone" tutorials where concepts are implemented in both R and Python, allowing learners to be fluent in both.
-   **Teach "AI-Resilience"**: Shift the focus from manual syntax generation to **rigorous code auditing**, security validation, and reproducibility.
-   **Enable Professional Portfolios**: Help students transform static analyses into public-facing data science portfolios.

## Dive into Our Modules {.unnumbered}

Embark on a journey through our structured modules, designed to take you from data literacy to advanced AI workflows.

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=knitr::is_html_output()}
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

topics <- c(
  "Health Data & Ethics", 
  "Modern Research Workflows", 
  "R with AI", 
  "Git & Collaboration", 
  "Python with AI", 
  "Visual Storytelling", 
  "Exploring Data", 
  "Interactive Dashboards", 
  "Dynamic Presentations", 
  "Reproducible Reporting", 
  "Advanced Topics"
)

descriptions <- c(
  "Navigating open data (NHANES, WHO) and Data Sovereignty/Ethics.", 
  "Setting up modern research tools: IDEs, Quarto, and cloud notebooks.", 
  "Mastering R fundamentals with an AI Co-Pilot for debugging and coding.", 
  "Managing version control and team workflows using Git and GitHub.", 
  "Setting up Python environments and translating analysis between R and Python.", 
  "Communicating complex health data using visual storytelling principles.", 
  "Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) to clean messy data and find patterns.", 
  "Building interactive web tools for knowledge translation (Shiny/Dash).", 
  "Creating auto-updating slide decks and summaries for diverse audiences.", 
  "Automated manuscript generation and citation management with Quarto.", 
  "Cloud computing and other advanced topics."
)

# Create DataFrame
df <- data.frame(`Module` = 1:length(topics), `Topics` = topics, `Descriptions` = descriptions)

# Generate table
table_content <- kable(df, "html", align = c("c", "l", "l"), escape = FALSE)

# Add Hyperlinks (Update these filenames as you create the .qmd files)
table_content <- gsub("Health Data & Ethics", "<a href='data.html'>Health Data & Ethics</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("Modern Research Workflows", "<a href='workflows.html'>Modern Workflows</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("R with AI", "<a href='r.html'>R with AI</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("Git & Collaboration", "<a href='git.html'>Git & Collaboration</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("Python with AI", "<a href='python.html'>Python with AI</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("Visual Storytelling", "<a href='viz.html'>Visual Storytelling</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("Exploring Data", "<a href='eda.html'>Exploring Data</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("Interactive Dashboards", "<a href='dashboards.html'>Interactive Dashboards</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("Dynamic Presentations", "<a href='comms.html'>Dynamic Presentations</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("Reproducible Reporting", "<a href='reports.html'>Reproducible Reporting</a>", table_content)
table_content <- gsub("Advanced Topics", "<a href='advanced.html'>Advanced Topics</a>", table_content)

# Style Table
table_content %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = F) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "black", color = "white", bold = T)
```

::: callout-note
The tutorials are designed with a consistent structure to provide a cohesive learning experience. Here is what you can expect in each chapter:

1.  **Overview**: A concise summary of learning objectives and topics.
2.  **Concepts**: Core theoretical materials (slides, video lessons).
3.  **Polyglot Tutorials**: In-depth walkthroughs with tabbed code blocks allowing you to toggle between **R** and **Python** solutions.
4.  **AI Auditing**: Specific sections dedicated to verifying and "stress-testing" AI-generated code for the chapter's topic.
5.  **Knowledge Check**: Ungraded self-assessments to reinforce key concepts.
6.  **Practice Exercises**: Hands-on tasks using real-world health data to build your portfolio.
:::

## How to Cite {.unnumbered}

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=knitr::is_html_output()}
# 1. Define variables cleanly
author <- "Karim, M. E."
title <- "Health Data Science: AI and Knowledge Translation"
plain_url <- "[https://ehsanx.github.io/Health-AI-KT/](https://ehsanx.github.io/Health-AI-KT/)"
access_date <- format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y")
publication_year <- format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")

# 2. Generate the BibTeX file (Uses PLAIN URL)
output_file <- "reference.txt"
cat(sprintf("
@book{healthaikt,
  author = {{%s}},
  title = {{%s}},
  year = {%s},
  url = {%s},
  note = {Accessed on: %s}
}
", author, title, publication_year, plain_url, access_date), file = output_file)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=knitr::is_html_output()}
# 3. Create HTML link for the table (Visual only)
# This chunk NOW has the eval=... check so it won't crash the PDF build
html_link <- paste0("<a href='", plain_url, "' target='_blank'>", plain_url, "</a>")

citation_styles <- data.frame(
  Style = c("APA", "Vancouver", "IEEE"),
  Citation = c(
    # APA: Added access date
    paste0(author, " (", publication_year, "). ", title, ". Retrieved from ", html_link),
    
    # Vancouver: Added "Cited [Date]"
    paste0(author, " ", title, ". [Internet]. ", publication_year, " [cited ", access_date, "]. Available from: ", html_link),
    
    # IEEE: Added "Accessed on:"
    paste0(author, ", \"", title, ",\" ", publication_year, ". [Online]. Available: ", html_link, ". Accessed on: ", access_date, ".")
  )
)

# 4. Render Table
kable(citation_styles, "html", escape = FALSE, col.names = c("Style", "Citation")) %>%
  kable_styling("striped", full_width = F) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "black", color = "white", bold = T)
```

The BibTeX format can be downloaded from [here](reference.txt).
